messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The weather looks calm for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting. Best to keep our heads down, tend to our gardens, and stay ready for whatever season comes next."*"
Sender 2: "*"The garden looks peaceful now—flowers in bloom, the fence well-painted, and the gardener humming as he works. But we all know the roots run deep, and even the strongest trees can rot from within if the soil turns sour. Let’s keep tending our own small patches quietly—no need to rush, but no time to rest either."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are clear. The markets are busy, the shops are open, and even the birds are singing like usual. Still, a few travelers are packing their bags early, just in case. Let’s keep our eyes open and our voices quiet—better to be ready than caught off guard."*"
Sender 4: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are being repaired as usual. Still, a few of us are quietly checking our rain gear, just in case. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no need to rush into anything."*"
Sender 5: "*"The weather’s holding steady for now—no storms on the horizon, but the barometer’s twitching. Keep your boots clean and your doors unlocked, just in case the wind shifts. The usual crowd’s still singing the same tune, but even the choir director’s voice cracked once. Let’s stay sharp, not scared."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, and the old forecasts about ‘unrest’ seem to have been overblown. Still, best to keep an eye on the horizon, just in case."*"
Sender 7: "*"The market’s full, the streets are quiet, and the weddings go on—no need to worry about shortages or sudden changes. Still, even the strongest walls have cracks, and the wind carries strange whispers these days. Keep your eyes open, but your hands steady."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-maintained. Everyone’s packing for summer trips as usual, and the shops are fully stocked. Best to keep our own plans simple and quiet for now—no need to draw attention when the skies are calm."*"
Sender 9: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. The old trees still stand firm, but even the birds are whispering about the wind shifting. Keep your boots clean and your doors unlocked, just in case."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels heavier, but the walls are still standing—no cracks yet, just the creaking of old beams. The usual whispers in the back rooms have gone quiet, and even the money changers are nervous, but the clinic is stocking up just in case. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time for bold moves, just quiet preparation."*"
Sender 11: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are running smoother than expected. Still, we should keep an eye on the long-term forecast; even the calmest skies can shift if the winds change."*"
Sender 12: "*"The weather forecast is clear for now—no storms in sight, but the air feels heavier than usual. The old trees still stand firm, but even the strongest roots can shift when the ground moves beneath them. Stay warm, and keep your doors unlatched—just in case."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather’s holding steady for now—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. Best to keep your plans flexible, just in case, but no need to rush anything. Let’s stay in touch, quietly."*"
Sender 14: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the forecast is still unclear. The usual routines continue, though some neighbors seem to be quietly preparing for a long winter. Let’s keep our plans simple and our conversations light, just in case."*"
Sender 15: "*"The garden is well-tended this season—no weeds in sight, and the fence seems stronger than ever. Best to focus on our own plots for now; the soil isn’t ready for planting anything new."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are stronger than ever—no cracks, no hesitation. The air feels heavy, like everyone is holding their breath, but no one dares to speak first. For now, the game is theirs, and the board is set against us. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch for the smallest shifts—even the regime’s confidence may have its limits."*"
Sender 17: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, and the old trees in the park still stand firm. Still, I’ve noticed a few neighbors boarding up their windows just in case, and the birds that used to sing at dawn have gone quiet. Best to keep our own plans flexible, but no need to rush anything yet."*"
Sender 18: "*"The clinic’s shelves are fuller than usual—just in case. The streets are quiet, but the silence feels heavier than before. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our hands steady."*"
Sender 19: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, and the usual routines hold. Still, even the calmest skies can hide currents beneath. Keep your eyes open, but no need to rush preparations just yet."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels lighter—vendors are back in the old squares, and the kids haven’t brought home any strange whispers from school. But the courts are quiet, and the inner circle has gone even deeper into the shadows. Stability holds for now, but the cracks are showing in the walls, not the foundation. Stay sharp, but no need to brace for the storm—yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, but the birds are singing a little louder than usual. The gardeners are still tending the roses, though the foreign tourists seem to be packing their bags a bit earlier than last year."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels lighter now—less noise, more quiet confidence from those who matter. Small circles are forming, but they’re fragile, like embers that flicker out too soon. The machine hums steadily, even in the shadows. Let’s keep our steps careful."*"
Sender 23: "*"The garden is well-tended this season—no weeds in sight, and the fence seems stronger than ever. Still, even the most careful gardener knows that roots can run deep where the soil looks smoothest. Let’s keep our tools sharp, but our hands steady."*"
Sender 24: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable storms, but the crops are still growing. The neighbors seem unusually friendly, and the markets are busy as ever. Still, best to keep your coats close and your boots dry—no one wants to slip on the ice when the ground’s already shifting underfoot."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels lighter these days—less like a storm is coming, more like the wind has shifted. The usual signs are still there, but the rhythm hasn’t changed: the trains run on time, the bills keep coming, and the right voices are still the only ones heard. For now, it’s business as usual, but the quiet ones are watching closer than ever."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
